intro.title: Build runtime validator and inferred type bridge
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple runtime validator function that checks data at runtime and uses TypeScript's type inference to create a static type from it. You'll learn how to write a validator using basic TypeScript constructs like type predicates and generics. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system and functions. By the end, you'll have a bridge that ensures runtime safety and provides accurate static types for your data.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential when building data-intensive applications like admin dashboards or analytics platforms where you need to validate API responses at runtime while maintaining TypeScript's type safety. For example, when displaying user data tables with filters, you can validate incoming JSON from external APIs against a schema, then automatically infer TypeScript types for the validated data. This ensures your UI components receive properly typed data for rendering charts, tables, or forms while catching data format errors early. Developers use this bridge pattern to create robust applications that handle unpredictable external data sources while maintaining development-time type checking and autocomplete.
